conversation:
Patient: I'm 58 years old, and I'm here because I've been having some vision changes, especially in my right eye. I have trouble adjusting to dim lighting, and straight lines sometimes look wavy to me, like the paneling in my office. It's been going on for a few months and seems to be getting worse.
Doctor: Have you experienced any pain, redness, or floaters in your right eye? Have you had any prior eye conditions, treatments, or family history of eye diseases? Have you recently experienced any trauma or exposure to bright light?
Patient: No, I haven't had any pain, redness, or floaters in my right eye. I don't recall having any prior eye conditions or treatments, and I don't think there's a family history of eye diseases that I'm aware of. I don't remember any recent trauma or exposure to bright light.
Doctor: Have you noticed any changes in your left eye as well, or is the vision change limited to the right eye?
Patient: The vision changes have been limited to my right eye. My left eye hasn't had any issues like the wavy lines or trouble adjusting to the dark. I haven't noticed any problems with my left eye at all.
Doctor: Have you undergone any previous ocular exams, such as a dilated eye exam or optical coherence tomography (OCT), and if so, what were the findings?
Patient: I don't recall having any previous ocular exams like a dilated eye exam or an OCT. I wasn't aware I needed one until today.
Doctor: Have you noticed any other symptoms related to your vision changes, such as flashes of light, floaters, or a sudden loss of vision in the right eye?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any flashes of light, floaters, or a sudden loss of vision in my right eye. The changes have been more gradual, like things looking wavy or having trouble seeing clearly in the dark, but nothing sudden or with bright flashes.
Doctor: Have you experienced any headaches, eye pain, or a loss of vision in your visual field associated with the wavy vision or trouble adjusting to dim lighting?
Patient: No, I haven't had any headaches or eye pain associated with the wavy vision or trouble adjusting to dim lighting. The main issue is just the vision changes, like things looking crooked or having a hard time seeing in the dark, but nothing else.
Doctor: Have you been diagnosed with diabetes, hypertension, or any other systemic condition that could affect your eyes?
Patient: Yes, I was diagnosed with high blood pressure a while back, and I know I haven't been taking my medication as I should. I’ve been meaning to get back on track with that, but it’s been slipping my mind.
Doctor: Has the patient undergone any recent blood tests, particularly for diabetes or lipid profile, which could be relevant to ocular health?
Patient: I don't recall having any recent blood tests for diabetes or a lipid profile. I know I should probably get checked, but I haven't made time for it yet.
Doctor: Have you noticed any recent changes in your vision clarity or field in either eye, and have you experienced any flashes of light or floaters in the affected eye?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any recent changes in my vision clarity or field in either eye beyond what we've already talked about, and I haven't experienced any flashes of light or floaters in the affected eye. It's mostly the wavy lines and trouble seeing in the dark that I've been dealing with.
Doctor: Have you undergone any recent blood tests for diabetes or a lipid profile? If not, would you be willing to schedule these tests to better understand your risk factors for ocular conditions?
Patient: I don't recall having any recent blood tests for diabetes or a lipid profile. I know I should probably get checked, but I haven't made time for it yet.
Doctor: Have you experienced any recent changes in your vision clarity or field in either eye beyond what we've already discussed, and have you noticed any flashes of light or floaters in the affected eye?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any recent changes in my vision clarity or field in either eye beyond what we've already talked about, and I haven't noticed any flashes of light or floaters in the affected eye. It's mostly the wavy lines and trouble seeing in the dark that I've been dealing with.
Doctor: Have you undergone any recent blood tests for diabetes or a lipid profile?
Patient: I don't recall having any recent blood tests for diabetes or a lipid profile. I know I should probably get checked, but I haven't made time for it yet.
Doctor: Have you noticed any recent changes in your vision, such as increased blurriness, loss of central vision, or difficulty reading?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any recent changes in my vision like increased blurriness or difficulty reading beyond what we've already talked about. It's still mostly the wavy lines and trouble seeing in the dark that I've been dealing with.
Doctor: Have you undergone any previous ocular examinations, such as a dilated eye exam or optical coherence tomography (OCT), even if not recently?
Patient: No, I don't recall having any previous ocular examinations like a dilated eye exam or an OCT. I haven't really thought about it much, to be honest. I just noticed the changes in my vision and came in for this consultation.
Doctor: Could you please describe the exact location of the wavy vision in your right eye? For example, is it in the center, the periphery, or does it affect your entire field of vision?
Patient: The wavy vision is mostly in the center of my right eye, especially when I look at straight lines like the paneling in my office. It makes things look crooked or wavy, and it's been getting worse over the last few months. It doesn't affect my whole field of vision, just the middle part.
